reviews.title: Great Panel for Comp Gaming even AAA
reviews.comment:
Bought this for about 180 USD during a black friday sale and im sure there are other sales that get run close to that, so this will be written looking at it from that price point. Which for the price it is great. 1440p 300hz is exactly where you want to be if you want the best possible looking game with the best speed. 4k in 2026 just doesnt make sense especially for games like overwatch and valorant even fortnite. So cutting it back to 1440p lets you actually hit that 300fps. The image is great, the pixel density isnt that bad for a 27in panel when viewing 1080p content. Even color accuracy isnt bad. Again, its a more budget end monitor but it gives you the amazing performance of an endgame
monitor.
Works well with any setup too, used it as a mass media consumption monitor with old games, so it works and is compatible with older stuff, and now am using it again for my 5070 build and competitive games. The size is also great, not too big that you need to move your full head but enough that you lean back and dont kiss the screen. Have been using it for almost a year now and its held up great so its even durable and doesn't scratch easy (it doesnt protect from user error as do most monitors.
reviews.author: Marina L.

reviews.title: Excellent. Look no further.
reviews.comment:
This review is for the 27" 1440p 300hz flat(not curved) variant.
This is an absolute banger deal. If you're on the fence, get it. This is the one. Heads up, though- pretty sure there aren't built in speakers. Having that said, this is still the best bang for your buck. The colors are nice and vibrant, and the settings offer decent tuning for gaming.
Very few affordable monitors support HDMI 2.1 and Display Port 1.4. This means your modern gaming systems like PS5 or a gaming PC can utilize their maximum potential. I use both. My PC gets 1440p at up to 300hz using HDMI 2.1, and this also supports HDR(you have to turn it on in the settings, default is off).
I bought two because this deal is just unreal.
